subject: orca
title: Orcas Snap Off Kelp and Use It to Scrub Each Other

scenes.text: Orcas were filmed making tools. No sea mammal had ever been seen doing that.
Off the Pacific Northwest, they snap the tip off a stalk of bull kelp.
Then two whales press it between their bodies and roll it back and forth.
Drones caught it on eight of 12 days, in every family group, young and old.
Whales with more peeling skin did it more, so it may work like a scrub.
Close relatives paired up most. A back scrub, with a tool they made themselves.

description:
Southern resident killer whales break off bull kelp stalks and roll them between their bodies to groom each other, the first tool-making ever reported in a marine mammal.
Drone footage showed it in every social group, both sexes and all ages, often between close relatives. Whales with more dead or molting skin groomed more, and the kelp may also help bonds (Current Biology, 2025). Fewer than 80 of these orcas remain.
What other tool could an orca invent?
first_comment: Scientists call it allokelping. Which animal do you think will be caught using tools next?
